safi-cedvel:75-80.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive (لا) redundant (zāʾida) [Note: This is the clearest of the i'rab analyses ... and it was said that it is a negation, the negated element being omitted, i.e. "so the unbeliever's claim is not sound; I swear ..."; and it was said that it is the lām of ibtidāʾ (commencement)], (بمواقع) attached to (أقسم), (الواو) parenthetical (اللام) for emphasis (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle (عظيم) naʿt (adjective) of قسم, nominative (لقرآن) like لقسم (في كتاب) attached to a second naʿt of (قرآن), (لا) negative (إلّا) for restriction (تنزيل) naʿt of قرآن, nominative like it [Note: or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هو", and the clause is an explanatory resumption], (من ربّ) attached to تنزيل ...
Clause: «أقسم ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive. Clause: «إنّه لقسم ... » has no grammatical position, parenthetical between the oath and its response. Clause: «لو تعلمون ... » has no grammatical position, parenthetical between the naʿt and the described noun ...
The jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. Clause: «انّه لقرآن ... » has no grammatical position, the response to the oath. Clause: «لا يمسّه إلّا المطهّرون» is in the position of nominative, naʿt of لقرآن.

* Morphology:
(75) مواقع: plural of موقع, a noun of place from the triliteral verb وقع; its wazn is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn, because it is a mithāl (assimilated) weak verb; the wazn of مواقع is مفاعل ...
(76) قسم: a ism maṣdar (noun standing for the verbal noun) from the quadriliteral أقسم; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas. (79) المطهّرون: plural of المطهّر ... a passive participle from the quadriliteral طهّر; its wazn is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.

* Benefits:
- The redundant (لا) ...
It enters speech merely to strengthen and emphasize it, as in the words of the Exalted ما مَنَعَكَ إِذْ رَأَيْتَهُمْ ضَلُّوا أَلَّا تَتَّبِعَنِ and ما مَنَعَكَ أَلَّا تَسْجُدَ, which is clarified by the other verse ما مَنَعَكَ أَنْ تَسْجُدَ. Among its redundant uses is the saying of the Exalted لِئَلَّا يَعْلَمَ أَهْلُ الْكِتابِ, i.e. "so that they may know" ...
The grammarians differed concerning the (لا) that occurs in the revelation in such words as the saying of the Exalted: لا أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ. It was said: it is a negation, and these differed over what it negates, in two ways. The first: it is something that came before, namely their denial and rejection. It was said to them: the matter is not as you say; then the oath is begun anew. The second: that what it negates is أقسم, on the basis that it is a report and not an inshāʾ (performative utterance); al-Zamakhsharī chose this and said: the meaning is that one swears by a thing only to magnify it, as the proof فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِمَواقِعِ النُّجُومِ، وَإِنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ; it is as if it were said: magnifying it by swearing by it is no magnification at all, i.e. it deserves a magnification above that.
- And it was said: it is redundant, and these differed over its benefit, in two views:
1- It was added to prepare for the negation of the response; the estimation is: "I do not swear by the Day of Resurrection; they will not be left aimless", and similar is the saying of the Exalted فَلا وَرَبِّكَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ حَتَّى يُحَكِّمُوكَ فِيما شَجَرَ بَيْنَهُمْ.
2- It was added merely for emphasis and to strengthen the speech, as in the saying of the Exalted لِئَلَّا يَعْلَمَ أَهْلُ الْكِتابِ.
The second place: the saying of the Exalted: قُلْ تَعالَوْا أَتْلُ ما حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَلَّا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئاً. It was said that (لا) is a negation; it was said it is prohibitive; and it was said it is redundant. All are possible.
The ruling on touching the Qur'an..
Ibn ʿAbbās used to forbid allowing a non-Muslim to touch the Qur'an or recite it. Al-Farrāʾ said: only one who believes in it finds its taste and benefit. A group said: the meaning of the verse is: none touches it except those purified from minor impurities and from major impurity (janāba). The apparent form of the verse is a negation, but its meaning is a prohibition. They said: it is not permitted for one in a state of janāba, nor for a menstruating woman, nor for one in a state of minor impurity (one without ablution) to carry the muṣḥaf or touch it. This is the view of ʿAṭāʾ, Ṭāwūs, Sālim, al-Qāsim and most of the people of knowledge. Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī and most jurists said it, and what indicates it is what
Mālik narrated in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Abī Bakr, that in the letter which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm: "Do not touch the Qur'an except in a state of purity." Mālik transmitted it as a mursal report. This ḥadīth has also come as a connected (mawṣūl) report, from Abū Bakr ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote this to the people of Yemen.
The sound view is that it is mursal. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also forbade travelling with the Qur'an to the land of the enemy. Al-Ḥakam, Ḥammād and Abū Ḥanīfa said: it is permitted for one in minor impurity or janāba to carry the muṣḥaf and touch it by its cover, and the jurists permitted one in minor impurity, janāba, or menstruation to carry a tafsīr of the muṣḥaf if the words of the tafsīr exceed the words of the muṣḥaf. On this basis it is permitted for these to carry the Tafsīr of (al-Jalālayn) or (Tafsīr wa-Bayān Mufradāt al-Qur'an), because the words of the tafsīr exceed the words of the muṣḥaf.
Likewise, one in janāba and a menstruating woman may not recite the Qur'an, even from memory, without touching it, though they may run it through their minds and thoughts without speaking or moving the tongue. The sounder view among the Ḥanafīs is that there is no harm in a menstruating or postpartum woman learning the Qur'an if it is word by word. As for the Mālikīs, they permitted the menstruating and postpartum woman to recite the Qur'an and touch the muṣḥaf for recitation, out of the need of teaching or for fear of forgetting. As for one without ablution, he may recite the Qur'an as long as he does not touch it.

safi-cedvel:81-82.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for rebuking interrogation (الفاء) resumptive (بهذا) attached to the khabar (مدهنون), (رزقكم) first mafʿūl bihi, accusative, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "gratitude for your provision" ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أنكم تكذّبون) is in the position of accusative, second mafʿūl bihi ...
Clause: «أنتم مدهنون ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive. Clause: «تجعلون ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the khabar (مدهنون). Clause: «تكذّبون ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of أنّ.

* Morphology:
(مدهنون), plural of مدهن, an active participle from the quadriliteral أدهن, meaning "to flatter, to placate, to be gentle"; its wazn is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:83-87.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive (لولا) a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); the fāʿil of (بلغت) is omitted, indicated by the context of the noble verse, i.e. the spirit or the soul (إذا) an adverbial stripped of conditional force, most probably, attached to an implied verb, i.e. "you would return it" (الواو) circumstantial (حينئذ) an adverbial annexed to an indeclinable adverbial, in the position of accusative, attached to (تنظرون), (الواو) circumstantial - or parenthetical - (إليه) attached to (أقرب), and likewise (منكم), (الواو) conjunction (لكن) for istidrāk (rectification), without effect (لا) negative (الفاء) resumptive (لولا) like the first (كنتم) a past verb, indeclinable, in the position of jussive, protasis, in both places [Note: Summary of the meaning of the noble verse: if you are truthful in denying the resurrection, then return the spirit of the dying man to his body so that death is removed from him and thus the resurrection is negated ...] ...
Clause: «بلغت الحلقوم ... » is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi [Note: It is possible that (إذا) contains the meaning of a condition, in which case the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the apodosis of the coming (إن)]. Clause: «أنتم ... تنظرون» is in the position of accusative, ḥāl. Clause: «تنظرون ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم). Clause: «نحن أقرب ... » is in the position of accusative, ḥāl [Note: or parenthetical]. Clause: «لا تبصرون» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause تنظرون. Clause: «كنتم غير مدينين» has no grammatical position, resumptive. Clause: «ترجعونها ... » has no grammatical position, explicative of the first implied apodosis, i.e.: "if you are not to be held to account, then return the dying spirit" [Note: It is possible that the protasis clause and its apodosis are parenthetical, and the clause ترجعونها is the apodosis of (إذا) if it is taken to contain the meaning of a condition]. Clause: «كنتم صادقين ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive ... The apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "if you are truthful in what you claim of there being no resurrection, then return the spirit of the dying man to his body so that death is removed from him."

* Morphology:
(83) الحلقوم: the name of the well-known organ (the throat); its wazn is فعلول with ḍamma on the fāʾ and the lām, with a sākin between them. (86) مدينين: plural of مدين, a passive participle from (دان، يدين), so it is of the wazn مبيع; it has an iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion: the wāw of مفعول was deleted because of the meeting of two sākins, after the ḍamma of the yāʾ was moved to the dāl, then the dāl was given kasra for harmony ...

* Rhetoric:
Implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in the saying of the Exalted فَلَوْلا إِذا بَلَغَتِ الْحُلْقُومَ.
Here the spirit is likened to a corporeal object that reaches the throat in a perceptible motion.

safi-cedvel:88-91.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive, consequential (أمّا) a particle of condition and elaboration (كان) an incomplete past verb, in the position of jussive, protasis of (إن), and its ism is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو", i.e. the deceased (من المقرّبين) attached to the khabar of كان (الفاء) connecting the apodosis [Note: which is the first condition (أمّا) ... this is because when two conditions are combined and only one apodosis is mentioned, the apodosis belongs to the first ... another reason for making it the apodosis of (أمّا) is that its protasis is omitted, so if the apodosis were omitted too, it would suffer injustice. And al-Amīr in his marginal gloss on al-Mughnī says: "It is possible that the apodosis belongs to the second, i.e. (إن)."], (روح) mubtadaʾ, nominative, its khabar omitted and preceding it, i.e. "for him is comfort" [Note: or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "so his recompense is comfort"
(2, 3, 4) as in the marginal note in the previous page, number (1).], (الواو) conjunction in the three places (أمّا إن ... اليمين) like its counterpart (الفاء) connecting the apodosis «2», (سلام) mubtadaʾ, nominative, its khabar being (لك), (من أصحاب) attached to the implied "being settled" (istiqrār).
Clause: «كان من المقرّبين....» has no grammatical position, resumptive. Clause: «له روح ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of (أمّا) «3» ... The apodosis of إن is omitted, indicated by what is mentioned. Clause: «كان من أصحاب ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause كان من المقرّبين.
Clause: «سلام لك ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of أمّا «4» ... The apodosis of إن is omitted, indicated by what is mentioned.

* Morphology:
(89) روح: a maṣdar meaning rest (istirāḥa); its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn. In al-Qāmūs: al-rawḥ with fatḥa is rest, mercy and the breeze of the wind. (الريحان), a noun meaning mercy and provision - as in al-Mukhtār - its wazn is فعلان, with the wāw turned into yāʾ contrary to the rule ... or فيعلان, i.e. ريوحان, because its diminutive is رويحين; when the yāʾ and the wāw met, the first being sākin, the wāw was turned into yāʾ, then assimilated into the second yāʾ, so it became ريّحان - with doubled yāʾ - then the yāʾ was lightened to ease the pronunciation, so it became ريحان. Some said that the word contains only one yāʾ and there is neither substitution nor assimilation, as proved by its plural رياحين and its diminutive رييحين.

safi-cedvel:92-94.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (أمّا إن كان ... من حميم) the i'rab of its counterpart has already been given [Note: in verses (88, 89) of this sūra], (من حميم) attached to a naʿt of (نزل), (الواو) conjunction ...

* Morphology:
(تصلية), a regular maṣdar from the quadriliteral صلّى, meaning "to burn":
and the (تاء) in it is a compensation for the yāʾ of the pattern تفعيل, which was deleted for heaviness; its wazn is تفعلة

safi-cedvel:95-96.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition (سبّح ... العظيم) its i'rab has already been given [Note: in verse (74) of this sūra ... and the verb سبّح is sometimes transitive by itself, as in the saying of the Exalted: سبّح اسم ربّك الأعلى (al-Aʿlā 1), and sometimes by a preposition, as in this verse, so there is no justification for claiming that the bāʾ is redundant ... and the bāʾ may be one of association (mulābasa).], (العظيم) naʿt of اسم, or of ربّك, genitive. Clause: «إنّ هذا لهو ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive. Clause: «هو حقّ ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of إنّ. Clause: «سبّح ... » is in the position of jussive, apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: "if the matter of Allah regarding reward and punishment is as mentioned, then glorify with the name ..."

safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(إذا) is a particle with several possibilities, the most evident being that it is an adverb of future time carrying the meaning of a condition, attached to the implied apodosis [Note: among the ways of parsing it: 1- It is an adverb stripped of the conditional sense, attached to the negation contained in ليس, i.e. "there is no denial of its occurrence when it occurs", that is, the denial is negated. 2- It is an adverb attached to the active participle رافعة, i.e. "it is one that raises, one that lowers, when it occurs" - said by Abū l-Baqāʾ. 3- Its apodosis is the following رجّت, so it is attached to it, and the (إذا) in it is a substitute or an emphasis. 4- It is a noun of time, a direct object of an omitted verb whose implied form is "remember" - and this is a weak opinion]. (لوقعتها) is attached to the predicate of ليس. (خافضة، رافعة) are two predicates of an omitted subject, its implied form being "it" (هي). The clause «وقعت الواقعة ...» is in the position of the genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi ... The apodosis of the condition is omitted, its implied form being "it lowered some peoples and raised others". The clause «ليس لوقعتها كاذبة» has no grammatical position, being resumptive - or parenthetical. The clause «(هي) خافضة ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption - or an explanation of the apodosis.

* Morphology:
(الواقعة): the Resurrection (al-qiyāma), which came in the pattern of the active participle, the tāʾ being for intensiveness. (وقعة): a maṣdar of single occurrence (maṣdar marra) from the triliteral وقع; its pattern is فعلة with a fatḥa and then a sukūn. (خافضة): feminine of خافض, an active participle from the triliteral خفض; its pattern is فاعل.

safi-cedvel:4-7.t:
* I'rab:
(إذا) is an adverb, a substitute (badal) for the first, and attached to what the first is attached to. (رجّا) is an accusative absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), and likewise (بسّا). (الفاء) is a conjunction, and the subject (ism) of (كانت) is a pronoun referring to the mountains. (الواو) is a conjunction. (ثلاثة) is an adjective of أزواج, accusative ...
The clause «رجّت الأرض ...» is in the position of the genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi. The clause «بسّت الجبال ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause رجّت. The clause «كانت هباء ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause بسّت. The clause «كنتم أزواجا ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause رجّت.

* Morphology:
(رجّا): an auditory maṣdar (maṣdar samāʿī) of the triliteral رجّ; its pattern is فعل with a fatḥa and then a sukūn, and its ʿayn and lām are from one letter. (بسّا): an auditory maṣdar of the triliteral بسّ, i.e. "he crumbled"; its pattern is فعل with a fatḥa and then a sukūn, and its ʿayn and lām are from one letter. (منبثّا): a passive participle of the quinqueliteral انبثّ; its pattern is منفعل with a ḍamma on the mīm and a fatḥa on the ʿayn, and the ʿayn and lām of the verb are from one letter. (ثلاثة): a name for the well-known number; it came in the feminine because the counted noun, أزواج, is masculine; its pattern is فعالة with a fatḥa on the first letter.

safi-cedvel:8-26.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive, for branching out (lil-tafrīʿ). (ما) is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative, a second subject (mubtadaʾ), its predicate being (أصحاب) that comes after it, and that is in the two verses ...
The clause «أصحاب الميمنة ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «ما أصحاب ...» is in the position of the nominative, the predicate of the subject أصحاب. The clause «أصحاب المشأمة ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause. The clause «ما أصحاب ...» is in the position of the nominative, the predicate of the (second) subject أصحاب.
10- 16- (الواو) is a conjunction. (السابقون) is a subject whose predicate is the clause أولئك المقرّبون [Note: it was said that its predicate is the second السابقون, i.e. "those who are foremost in good are foremost to Paradise", or something to that effect ... but the speech in this way requires a great deal of interpretation, so this parsing is the less preferred]. The second (السابقون) is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the first, nominative. (المقرّبون) is the predicate of the subject (أولئك) [Note: or a substitute for the demonstrative noun, and the predicate is (في جنّات)]. (في جنّات) is attached to a second predicate of the subject (أولئك) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in (المقرّبون) ... and it may be a fronted predicate of the subject ثلّة]. (ثلّة) is the predicate of an omitted subject, its implied form being "هم" (they), i.e. the foremost [Note: or it is a subject whose predicate is (على سرر ...)]. (من الأوّلين) is attached to an adjective of ثلّة. (من الآخرين) is an adjective of قليل. (على سرر) is attached to a second predicate of the subject "they" (هم). (متّكئين) is an accusative ḥāl from the pronoun of settledness (al-istiqrār) which is the predicate in His saying (على سرر). (عليها) is attached to (متّكئين). (متقابلين) is a second accusative ḥāl. The clause «السابقون ... أولئك المقرّبون» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause. The clause «أولئك المقرّبون ...» is in the position of the nominative, the predicate of the subject (السابقون). The clause «(هم) ثلّة ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption [Note: or in the position of the nominative, a second predicate of the subject (السابقون)].
17- 18- (عليهم) is attached to (يطوف). (بأكواب) is attached to (يطوف) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from ولدان]. (من معين) is an adjective of كأس ...
The clause «يطوف عليهم ولدان ..» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl from the pronoun in متقابلين.
19- 23- (لا) is a negation, and the (الواو) in (يصدّعون) is the deputy agent. (عنها) is attached to (يصدّعون), and the preposition is causal (sababiyya). (لا) is a negation, and the (الواو) in (ينزفون) is the agent. (فاكهة) is conjoined by the wāw to أكواب, genitive. (ممّا) is attached to an adjective of (فاكهة), and in the second case to an adjective of (لحم). (الواو) is a conjunction. (حور) is a subject, nominative, its predicate being omitted and fronted, its implied form being "for them" [Note: or conjoined to (ولدان)]. (كأمثال) is attached to a second adjective of (حور) ...
The clause «لا يصدّعون عنها ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl from كأس [Note: or a ḥāl from the pronoun in (عليهم), or it has no grammatical position, being resumptive]. The clause «لا ينزفون ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause لا يصدّعون. The clause «يتخيّرون ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the first relative noun (ما). The clause «يشتهون ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
24- (جزاء) is an accusative mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) [Note: or an absolute object of an omitted verb, i.e. "they are recompensed with a recompense"]. (ما) is a particle of the verbal noun [Note: or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted, and the clause after it a ṣila], and the interpreted maṣdar (ما كانوا ...) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (جزاء). The clause «كانوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle (ما) which forms a maṣdar. The clause «يعملون ...» is in the position of the accusative, the predicate of كانوا.
25- 26- (لا) is a negation. (فيها) is attached to (يسمعون). The second (لا) is redundant, for emphasising the negation. (تأثيما) is conjoined to (لغوا), accusative. (إلّا) is for exception. (قيلا) is accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). (سلاما) is a substitute for (قيلا) [Note: or a direct object of the maṣdar قيل ... or an absolute object of an omitted verb, the clause being the content of what is said], accusative. The second (سلاما) is a verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī) of the first, accusative like it.
The clause «لا يسمعون ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(8) الميمنة: a maṣdar mīmī ending in a tāʾ for intensiveness, from the triliteral يمن; its pattern is مفعلة with a fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn. (9) المشأمة: a maṣdar mīmī ending in a tāʾ for intensiveness, from the triliteral شأم; its pattern is مفعلة with a fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn. (13) ثلّة: a collective noun (ism jamʿ) meaning the group or the many; its pattern is فعلة with a ḍamma and then a sukūn, and the plural is ثلل with a kasra on the thāʾ. (15) موضونة: feminine of موضون, a passive participle from the triliteral وضن, meaning "he folded part of it over another and doubled its weave"; the "mawḍūna" coat of mail is the closely woven one, or that woven ring by ring in pairs. (17) ولدان: like صبيان, plural of وليد meaning "one born"; they are created in Paradise from the outset, according to the soundest views ...
(مخلّدون): plural of مخلّد, a passive participle from the quadriliteral خلّد; its pattern is مفعّل with a ḍamma on the mīm and a fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn. (18) أباريق: plural of إبريق, derived from البريق (gleam) for the clarity of its colour; its pattern is إفعيل; a vessel with a handle and a spout.

* Rhetoric:
The unrestricted, summarised simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal al-mujmal): in the saying of the Exalted كَأَمْثالِ اللُّؤْلُؤِ الْمَكْنُونِ.
Here He, glory be to Him, the Exalted, likened them to the pearl, that is, in clarity, and qualified it with "concealed" (al-maknūn), that is, hidden, because it is clearer and further from alteration. In the hadith: "Their clarity is like the clarity of the pearl that hands have not touched."

safi-cedvel:27-40.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (ما أصحاب اليمين) is like ما أصحاب الميمنة [Note: in verse (8) of this sūra]. (في سدر) is attached to the predicate of an omitted subject, its implied form being "هم" (they) [Note: or attached to a second predicate of the first أصحاب]. (لا) is a negation. (مقطوعة) is an adjective of فاكهة, genitive. The second (لا) is redundant and necessary. (ممنوعة) is conjoined by the wāw to مقطوعة, genitive ..
The clause «أصحاب اليمين ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «ما أصحاب ...» is in the position of the nominative, the predicate of the subject (أصحاب). The clause «(هم) في سدر ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption [Note: or in the position of the nominative, a second predicate of the subject أصحاب].
35- 40- (إنشاء) is an accusative absolute object. (أبكارا) is an accusative second direct object. (عربا، أترابا) are two adjectives of (أبكارا), accusative like it. (لأصحاب) is attached to (أنشأهنّ) [Note: or attached to (جعلناهنّ) ... or attached to (أترابا), meaning "equal to them in age"]. (ثلّة) is the predicate of an omitted subject, its implied form being "هم" (they). (من الأولين) is attached to an adjective of (ثلّة). (من الآخرين) is attached to an adjective of the second ثلة.
The clause «انّا أنشأناهنّ ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive [Note: the pronoun of the third person refers to the women of Paradise who are alluded to by "the couches" ... and it is possible that the clause is in the position of the genitive, an adjective of فرش]. The clause «أنشأناهنّ ...» is in the position of the nominative, the predicate of إنّ. The clause «جعلناهنّ ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause أنشأناهنّ. The clause «(هم) ثلة ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(28) مخضود: a passive participle from the triliteral خضد الشجر, meaning "he cut off its thorn"; its pattern is مفعول. (29) طلح: a name for the banana tree; its pattern is فعل with a fatḥa and then a sukūn. (30) ممدود: a passive participle from the triliteral مدّ; its pattern is مفعول. (31) مسكوب: a passive participle from the triliteral سكب; its pattern is مفعول. (33) ممنوعة: feminine of ممنوع, a passive participle from the triliteral منع; its pattern is مفعول. (35) إنشاء: a regular maṣdar (maṣdar qiyāsī) of the quadriliteral أنشأ; its pattern is إفعال. (37) عربا: plural of عروب with a fatḥa on the ʿayn, a name for a woman who is loving to her husband; the pattern of عرب is فعل with two ḍammas.

safi-cedvel:41-48.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (ما أصحاب ... ) is like the first [Note: in verse (8) of the sūra]. (في سموم) is like في سدر [Note: in verse (28) of the sūra]. (من يحموم) is attached to an adjective of (ظلّ). (لا) is a negation. (بارد) is an adjective of ظلّ, genitive. The second (لا) is redundant and necessary. (كريم) is conjoined to بارد by the wāw, genitive.
The clause «أصحاب الشمال ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «ما أصحاب ...» is in the position of the nominative, the predicate of the first subject (أصحاب). The clause «(هم) في سموم ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption [Note: or in the position of the nominative, a second predicate of أصحاب].
45- 48- (قبل) is an adverb of time, accusative, attached to the predicate (مترفين). (على الحنث) is attached to (يصرّون). (الهمزة) is for the interrogation of denial (istifhām inkārī) in the three places. (إذا) is an adverb of future time, in the position of the accusative, attached to an omitted element which is the apodosis, explained by the predicate of إنّ, i.e. "when we have died ... shall we be raised?" [Note: it is not permissible to attach it to (مبعوثون) - and consequently the nominal clause is not the apodosis of (إذا) - because what comes after (إنّ) does not operate on what comes before it]. (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis. (آباؤنا) is a subject, nominative, its predicate omitted, its implied form being "to be raised" [Note: the author of al-Kashshāf conjoined (آباؤنا) to the position of (إنّ and its noun), whose position is the nominative, so there is no need to imply the predicate].
The clause «إنّهم كانوا ...» has no grammatical position, being a justification of the preceding punishment. The clause «كانوا ... مترفين» is in the position of the nominative, the predicate of إنّ. The clause «كانوا يصرّون» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause كانوا ... مترفين. The clause «كانوا يقولون ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause كانوا ... مترفين. The clause «يصرّون ...» is in the position of the accusative, the predicate of كانوا. The clause «يقولون ...» is in the position of the accusative, the third predicate of كانوا. The clause «the condition, its verb and its apodosis ...» is in the position of the accusative, the content of what is said. The clause «متنا ...» is in the position of the genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi. The clause «كنّا ترابا ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause متنا. The clause «إنّا لمبعوثون ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption [Note: or explicative of the implied apodosis]. The clause «آباؤنا ... (مبعوثون)» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause إنّا لمبعوثون.

* Morphology:
(43) يحموم: a name for intense smoke; its pattern is يفعول. Al-ʿUkbarī said it is from الحمم (embers) or from الحميم (boiling water). (46) الحنث: a name for sin; and التحنّث is devotion in order to avoid sin; its pattern is فعل with a kasra and then a sukūn. The great sin (al-ḥinth al-ʿaẓīm) is polytheism (shirk).

* Rhetoric:
The art of precaution (fann al-iḥtirās): in the saying of the Exalted لا بارِدٍ وَلا كَرِيمٍ.
When He, glory be to Him, the Exalted, said وَظِلٍّ مِنْ يَحْمُومٍ, it might have suggested that the shade could bring them some relief after fatigue, so He negated from it two attributes of shade. He means: it is shade, but not like other shades. He called it shade, then negated from it the coolness of shade, its comfort and its benefit to one who takes refuge in it from the harm of heat, so as to wipe out what the meaning of "shade" implies of seeking comfort in it; the meaning is that it is a hot, harmful shade. In it is mockery of the people of the left, and that they do not deserve the cool, noble shade that is for their opposites in Paradise.

* Benefits:
When must (لا) be repeated.
In this verse occurs the saying of the Exalted وَظِلٍّ مِنْ يَحْمُومٍ لا بارِدٍ وَلا كَرِيمٍ, where (لا) is repeated. We shall clarify below when it must be repeated:
If what follows it is a nominal clause, its beginning definite or indefinite, and it (that is, لا) has not operated on it (i.e. the operation of إنّ or كان), or what follows it is a clause that begins with a past verb, in form or in implication, then it must be repeated. An example of the definite is لَا الشَّمْسُ يَنْبَغِي لَها أَنْ تُدْرِكَ الْقَمَرَ وَلَا اللَّيْلُ سابِقُ النَّهارِ وَكُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ.
An example of the past verb is the saying of the Exalted فَلا صَدَّقَ وَلا صَلَّى, and in the hadith: «فإنّ المنبّت لا أرضا قطع ولا ظهرا أبقى» ("the one who is cut off has neither traversed land nor spared a mount").
- If the intended speech is a supplication, the repetition is left out, as in our saying: لا شلّت يداك، ولا فضّ اللَّه فاك ("May your hands not be paralysed, and may Allah not break your mouth").
- Likewise it must be repeated if it enters upon a singular predicate, adjective or ḥāl, such as: (زيد لا شاعر ولا كاتب) ("Zayd is neither a poet nor a writer") and (جاء زيد لا ضاحكا ولا باكيا) ("Zayd came neither laughing nor weeping"), and as in the saying of the Exalted: إِنَّها بَقَرَةٌ لا فارِضٌ وَلا بِكْرٌ and وَظِلٍّ مِنْ يَحْمُومٍ لا بارِدٍ وَلا كَرِيمٍ and وَفاكِهَةٍ كَثِيرَةٍ لا مَقْطُوعَةٍ وَلا مَمْنُوعَةٍ and مِنْ شَجَرَةٍ مُبارَكَةٍ زَيْتُونَةٍ لا شَرْقِيَّةٍ وَلا غَرْبِيَّةٍ.
But if what it enters upon is an imperfect verb, its repetition is not required, as in the saying of the Exalted: قُلْ لا أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْراً

safi-cedvel:49-56.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis. (إلى ميقات) is attached to (مجموعون), since it is given the meaning "driven". The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «إنّ الأولين ... لمجموعون» is in the position of the accusative, the content of what is said.
51- 56- (أيّها) is an indefinite specific vocative (munādā nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative. (الضالّون) is a substitute (badal) for أي - or an explicative apposition (ʿaṭf bayān) to it - following it in the nominative in form. (لآكلون) is like لمجموعون. (من شجر) is attached to (آكلون). (من زقّوم) is attached to an adjective of شجر. (الفاء) is a conjunction in the three places. (منها) is attached to (مالئون). (البطون) is a direct object of the active participle مالئون. (عليه) is attached to (شاربون), and likewise (من الحميم). (شرب) is an absolute object, its operator being the active participle شاربون, accusative ... (يوم) is an accusative adverb attached to a ḥāl from (نزلهم). The clause «إنّكم ... لآكلون» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause of what is said. The clause of the vocative «أيّها الضّالون» has no grammatical position, being parenthetical. The clause «هذا نزلهم ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption.

* Morphology:
(51) المكذّبون: plural of المكذّب, an active participle of the quadriliteral كذّب; its pattern is مفعّل with a ḍamma on the mīm and a kasra on the doubled ʿayn. (55) شرب: an auditory maṣdar of the triliteral شرب; its pattern is فعل with a ḍamma and then a sukūn. (الهيم): plural of أهيم - which is the camel afflicted with thirst - and plural of هيماء ... The original in its plural is that it be on فعل with a ḍamma and then a sukūn, but the hāʾ was given a kasra to suit the yāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
The representational simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī): in the saying of the Exalted ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ أَيُّهَا الضَّالُّونَ الْمُكَذِّبُونَ، لَآكِلُونَ مِنْ شَجَرٍ مِنْ زَقُّومٍ، فَمالِؤُنَ مِنْهَا الْبُطُونَ. فَشارِبُونَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْحَمِيمِ، فَشارِبُونَ شُرْبَ الْهِيمِ.
He likened them in their drinking to thirsty camels that water does not quench, because of a disease that afflicts them resembling dropsy, so they keep gulping the drink until they perish or fall severely ill. The point of resemblance is that each of them drinks and is not satisfied, which urges it to seek more drink. [Translator's note: the source reads "تعب" (to be wearied) where "تعبّ" (to gulp) is evidently meant; translated as "gulping".]
The art of mockery (fann al-tahakkum): in the saying of the Exalted هذا نُزُلُهُمْ يَوْمَ الدِّينِ, where He called the kinds of punishment and the strokes of terrors a "hospitality" (nuzul), mocking them, because nuzul in reality is the provision prepared for the guest to honour him. This mockery is as in the saying of the Exalted فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ and as in the verse of Abū l-Shaʿrāʾ al-Ḍabbī:
وكنا إذا الجبار بالجيش ضافنا ... جعلنا القنا والمرهفات له نزولا
(When the tyrant came to us as a guest with his army, we made spears and sharp swords his hospitality.)

* Benefits:
- The simple fāʾ..
It occurs in three ways..
1- It is a conjunction and gives three meanings:
1- Order (tartīb), which is of two kinds: of meaning, as in (قام زيد فعمرو) ("Zayd stood up, then ʿAmr"), and of mention, which is conjoining the detailed to the summarised, as in the saying of the Exalted: فَأَزَلَّهُمَا الشَّيْطانُ عَنْها فَأَخْرَجَهُما مِمَّا كانا فِيهِ and فَقَدْ سَأَلُوا مُوسى أَكْبَرَ مِنْ ذلِكَ فَقالُوا أَرِنَا اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً.
2- Immediate succession (taʿqīb): it is in each thing according to its nature. Do you not see that it is said: (تزوّج فلان فولد له) ("So-and-so married and a child was born to him") when there was between the two nothing but the period of pregnancy? The Exalted said: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَتُصْبِحُ الْأَرْضُ مُخْضَرَّةً.
3- Causation (sababiyya): this is predominant in the fāʾ that conjoins a clause or an adjective. The clause, as in the saying of the Exalted فَوَكَزَهُ مُوسى فَقَضى عَلَيْهِ, and the adjective, as in the saying of the Exalted: لَآكِلُونَ مِنْ شَجَرٍ مِنْ زَقُّومٍ فَمالِؤُنَ مِنْهَا الْبُطُونَ فَشارِبُونَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْحَمِيمِ فَشارِبُونَ شُرْبَ الْهِيمِ.
2- The second way of the fāʾ: it connects the apodosis, as in the saying of the Exalted وَإِنْ يَمْسَسْكَ بِخَيْرٍ فَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ.
The apodosis of a condition must be accompanied by the fāʾ if it is a nominal clause, or a verbal clause whose verb is of request or is inert, or is accompanied by ما, لن, قد, the sīn or سوف, as in the saying of the Exalted إِنْ يَسْرِقْ فَقَدْ سَرَقَ أَخٌ لَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ.
3- The third way of the fāʾ: it is redundant (zāʾida), its entering into the speech being like its leaving it. Sībawayh does not affirm this, but al-Akhfash permitted its redundancy in the predicate without restriction, and gave the example «أخوك فوجد» ("your brother, so he was found"). Al-Farrāʾ, al-Aʿlam and a group restricted the permissibility to the predicate being a command or prohibition, as in the saying of the Exalted هذا فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ حَمِيمٌ وَغَسَّاقٌ and our saying (زيد فلا تضربه) ("Zayd - do not hit him").

safi-cedvel:57-62.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is a conjunction to connect the effect with the cause. (لولا) is a particle of urging. The second (الفاء) is resumptive. (الهمزة) is for interrogation. (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative, a first direct object. The second (الهمزة) is for the interrogation of denial. (أم) is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) meaning "rather" (bal) [Note: it may conjoin a clause to a clause by parsing (أنتم) as the agent of an omitted verb that is explained by the one mentioned, on account of the preference for a verbal clause coming after the interrogative hamza ... but this parsing is the less preferred] ...
The clause «نحن خلقناكم ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «خلقناكم ...» is in the position of the nominative, the predicate of the subject (نحن). The clause «تصدّقون» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to an implied resumption that is caused by what precedes, i.e. "be alert, then believe". The clause «رأيتم ...» has no grammatical position, being a resumption that confirms what precedes. The clause «تمنون ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما). The clause «أأنتم تخلقونه ...» is in the position of the accusative, a second direct object of the verb of seeing. The clause «تخلقونه ...» is in the position of the nominative, the predicate of the subject (أنتم). The clause «نحن الخالقون ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
60- 61- (بينكم) is attached to (قدّرنا). (الواو) is a conjunction. (ما) is a negation that operates as ليس. (مسبوقين) is genitive in form and accusative in position, the predicate of ما. (أن) is a particle of the verbal noun and of the accusative. (الواو) is a conjunction. (ننشئكم) is an accusative imperfect, conjoined to (نبدّل). (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نبدّل) is in the position of the genitive by (على), attached to (مسبوقين) [Note: it may be attached to (قدّرنا), i.e. "We decreed death among you in order that We replace". And the clause ما نحن بمسبوقين is parenthetical]. The clause «نحن قدّرنا ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption. The clause «قدّرنا ...» is in the position of the nominative, the predicate of the subject (نحن). The clause «ما نحن بمسبوقين ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause. The clause «نبدّل ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle (أن) which forms a maṣdar. The clause «ننشئكم ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause نبدّل. The clause «لا تعلمون ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
62- (الواو) is resumptive. (اللام) is the lām of the oath, for an implied oath. (قد) is a particle of verification. (الفاء) is a conjunction to connect the effect with the cause. (لولا تذكّرون) is like لولا تصدّقون. The clause «علمتم ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the implied oath ... The implied clause of oath has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «تذكّرون ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to an implied resumption that is caused by what precedes, i.e. "be alert, then remember".

* Morphology:
(58) تمنون: it has an elision weakening (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf): the lām of the verb - the yāʾ - was dropped because it met, quiescent, the wāw of the group. (60) مسبوقين: plural of مسبوق, a passive participle from the triliteral سبق; its pattern is مفعول. (أمثال) (61): it may be a plural of مِثل with a kasra and then a sukūn, a name for the equal; or a plural of مَثَل - with two fatḥas - a noun meaning attribute.

safi-cedvel:63-67.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive. (أرأيتم ... الزارعون) is like أرأيتم ... الخالقون [Note: in the two verses (58, 59) of this sūra]. (لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle. (اللام) occurs in the apodosis of لو. (حطاما) is an accusative second direct object. (الفاء) is a conjunction. (ظلتم) is a past verb from which one of the two lāms has been dropped for lightness. (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis. (بل) is for transitional abandonment (iḍrāb intiqālī) ...
The clause «رأيتم ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «تحرثون ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما). The clause «أنتم تزرعونه ...» is in the position of the accusative, a second direct object of the verb of seeing. The clause «تزرعونه ...» is in the position of the nominative, the predicate of the subject (أنتم). The clause «نحن الزارعون ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «نشاء ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption. The clause «جعلناه ...» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. The clause «ظلتم ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause جعلناه. The clause «تفكّهون ...» is in the position of the accusative, the predicate of ظلتم [Note: some made the verb (ظلتم) complete, meaning "you spent the day" - from الظلّ - so the clause تفكّهون is a ḥāl from the agent]. The clause «إنّا لمغرمون ...» is in the position of the accusative, the content of what is said of an implied saying, which is a ḥāl from the agent of تفكّهون. The clause «نحن محرومون ...» has no grammatical position, being a resumption within the scope of the saying.

* Morphology:
(46) الزارعون: plural of الزارع, an active participle from the triliteral زرع; its pattern is فاعل. [Translator's note: the source gives the number (46) here, but the word occurs in verse 64; this is a slip in the source.] (65) ظلتم: one of the two lāms is dropped for lightness; its original is ظللتم ... its pattern is فلتم with a fatḥa on the fāʾ and a sukūn on the lām. (تفكّهون): one of the two tāʾs is dropped, regularly. (66) مغرمون: plural of مغرم, a passive participle from the quadriliteral أغرم; its pattern is مفعل with a ḍamma on the mīm and a fatḥa on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:68-70.t:
* I'rab:
(أفرأيتم الماء. نحن المنزلون) is like أفرأيتم ما تمنون ... الخالقون [Note: in the two verses (58, 59) of the sūra, in words and clauses]. (من المزن) is attached to (أنزلتموه), and the (الواو) in (أنزلتموه) is redundant, a lengthening of the vowel of the mīm. (لو ... أجاجا) is like لو نشاء ... حطاما [Note: in verse (65) of the sūra]. (فلولا تشكرون) is like لولا تصدّقون [Note: in verse (57) ...]

* Morphology:
(المزن): plural of مزنة, a noun meaning the cloud; its pattern is فعلة with a ḍamma and then a sukūn, and likewise المزن is of the pattern فعل.

safi-cedvel:71-74.t:
* I'rab:
(أفرأيتم ... المنشئون) is like أفرأيتم ... الخالقون [Note: in the two verses (58, 59) of the sūra, in words and clauses.] (تذكرة) is an accusative second direct object. (للمقوين) is attached to (متاعا). (الفاء) is the connecting particle for the apodosis of an implied condition. (باسم) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of سبّح ...
The clause «نحن جعلناها ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption. The clause «جعلناها ...» is in the position of the nominative, the predicate of the subject (نحن). The clause «سبّح ...» is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if the power of Allah in creation, origination and ordering is as mentioned, then glorify with the name ...".

* Morphology:
(71) تورون: it has an elision weakening (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf) after a weakening by quiescence (iʿlāl bi-l-taskīn) ... its original is توريون - with a yāʾ after the rā' - the ḍamma on the yāʾ was heavy so it was made quiescent and the vowel was transferred to the rāʾ before it - weakening by quiescence - then the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, so it became تورون - weakening by elision; its pattern is تفعون.
(72) المنشئون: plural of المنشئ, an active participle of the quadriliteral أنشأ; its pattern is مفعل with a ḍamma on the mīm and a kasra on the ʿayn. (73) المقوين: plural of المقوي, meaning the traveller who alights in the qawā or the qiwāʾ, with a kasra on the qāf in both, which is the empty land far from habitation; an active participle of the quadriliteral أقوى ... it has an elision weakening: its original is المقويين - with two yāʾs - two quiescent letters met, the yāʾ that is the lām of the word was dropped, so it became المقوين; its pattern is المفعين ...
